description: Table 1 is a single rendered data table (a plain black-on-white grid with a header row and four data rows); a partially cropped line of heading text sits above the header row and is illegible. The columns, left to right, are Samples, YS, UTS, UE, TE, σ'_f, b and RMSE, where the caption defines YS as yield strength (MPa), UTS as ultimate tensile strength (MPa), UE as uniform elongation (%), TE as total elongation (%), σ'_f as fatigue strength coefficient, b as fatigue strength exponent and RMSE as the root mean square error of log10 Nf. The four rows are the conditions ST, 550-6, 600-6 and 650-6 of an Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1C (wt%) austenitic low-density steel. ST is the softest (YS 337 ± 32 MPa; UTS 784 ± 15 MPa) and by far the most ductile (UE 57.7 ± 1.3 %; TE 72.0 ± 0.8 %). All aged rows trade ductility for strength: 550-6 (YS 829 ± 17; UTS 1045 ± 8), 600-6 (YS 776 ± 19; UTS 1104 ± 17) and 650-6 (YS 579 ± 14; UTS 978 ± 4). 550-6 holds the highest YS, 600-6 the highest UTS, and 650-6 the lowest strength among the aged conditions. Fatigue parameters vary non-monotonically in σ'_f (1510, 2243, 1040, 1153) while b is negative for every row (−0.15, −0.17, −0.11, −0.12).

observations.observation: The table contains four sample rows labelled ST, 550-6, 600-6 and 650-6, and eight columns labelled Samples, YS, UTS, UE, TE, σ'_f, b and RMSE.
The ST condition has the lowest YS (337 ± 32 MPa) and lowest UTS (784 ± 15 MPa) of the four rows, while its ductility is the highest (UE 57.7 ± 1.3 %, TE 72.0 ± 0.8 %).
Row 550-6 lists the highest YS in the table, 829 ± 17 MPa, with UTS 1045 ± 8 MPa, UE 45.5 ± 1.4 % and TE 57.7 ± 0.4 %.
Row 600-6 lists the highest UTS in the table, 1104 ± 17 MPa, with YS 776 ± 19 MPa, UE 45.1 ± 1.5 % and TE 58.4 ± 1.4 %.
Row 650-6 is the weakest aged condition (YS 579 ± 14 MPa; UTS 978 ± 4 MPa) and has the lowest TE among all rows, 52.7 ± 1.6 %, while its UE (46.4 ± 1.2 %) is the highest of the three aged samples.
The fatigue strength coefficient σ'_f is printed as 1510 (ST), 2243 (550-6), 1040 (600-6) and 1153 (650-6), i.e. it is highest for 550-6 and lowest for 600-6, not monotonic with strength.
The fatigue strength exponent b is negative for every condition: −0.15 (ST), −0.17 (550-6), −0.11 (600-6) and −0.12 (650-6).
RMSE of log10 Nf is 0.0429 for ST, 0.0952 for 550-6, 0.1776 for 600-6 and 0.1139 for 650-6, so the scatter in fatigue-life fitting is smallest for ST and largest for 600-6.
A line of heading text immediately above the table header row is cut off by the image crop and cannot be read.

The caption states that the table reports tensile and fatigue properties of the ST, 550-6, 600-6 and 650-6 samples, and defines YS (MPa), UTS (MPa), UE (%), TE (%), σ'_f, b and RMSE (root mean square error of log10 Nf).

The citing text states that all aged conditions show significant increases in yield and ultimate tensile strengths but a reduction in ductility compared with the ST condition, consistent with the tabulated values.

The citing text attributes the strengthening to precipitation hardening by intragranular κ-carbides interacting with dislocations, and the diminished strength of 650-6 to grain-boundary weakening from serious intergranular κ-carbide precipitation.
The citing text reports fatigue strengths at 10^7 cycles of 157.5 MPa (ST), 162 MPa (550-6), 175.5 MPa (600-6) and 171 MPa (650-6); these values are not present in the table itself.
